subject: Intermittent p99 spikes on Hosted API — StarryAI production (16k context)
messages:
From: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@starryai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2029 08:14:02 -0700
Subject: Intermittent p99 spikes on Hosted API — StarryAI production (16k context)

Hi Marissa / Ben,

We started seeing elevated p99 latency in our production service this morning (~06:30 UTC). The mean latency is fine but p95/p99 are spiking to 2.3–4.1s for the same prompt set that previously stayed under 700ms. This only happens on calls with ~16k context windows — short-context calls look normal. We've also seen a handful of 504s during spikes.

Attached are a small bundle of request logs and an annotated latency spike PNG. Sample request ids: starry-req-21a, starry-req-21b. Happy to jump on a call if helpful — this is affecting real-time features for paying customers.

Thanks,
Jordan Miles
Senior Platform Engineer
StarryAI

Attachments: p99-spike-graphs.png (image/png), starry_request_logs.zip (text/zip)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2029 08:45:27 -0700
Subject: RE: Intermittent p99 spikes on Hosted API — StarryAI production (16k context)

Marissa / Ben — quick internal note (internal only):

Preliminary findings (5–10min triage):
- Correlation with StarryAI tenant traffic shows >80% of p99 events tied to requests with >12k tokens (consistent with their 16k window).
- KV cache eviction rate climbs sharply when large context requests are interleaved with other tenants — we see increased KV cache churn and larger per-request recompute cost.
- A small class of requests includes repeated long system messages + multi-document batches which force larger attention/kv footprints.

Short-term mitigations to propose to the customer:
1) Route 16k-context requests to a dedicated pool with higher memory and disabled aggressive sharing (temporary).
2) Apply a soft rate-limit per-tenant for >12k requests (e.g., 6rps burst cap) to prevent transient cascade.
3) Enable prefix/KV sticky caching for StarryAI for the next 2 hours (if ops approve).
4) As a fallback, configure automatic graceful downgrade to the 8k model variant for requests where truncation or summarization is acceptable.

Impact: these changes should reduce tail recompute and bring p99 closer to baseline within ~30–90 minutes. Risk: dedicated routing and sticky caching increase cost; doing automatic downgrades may change outputs (need customer sign-off).

I'm escalating to Neha for exec awareness — potential SLA visibility and credit discussion if we don't hit targets.

[1mLaura[0m
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Jordan — quick update and plan: we've approved a short-lived routing change and will enable tenant-sticky KV caching for StarryAI at 09:45 PDT. Ops will also apply a soft rate-limit of 6rps for requests >12k tokens to dampen bursts.

If you opt in, we can enable graceful fallback to the 8k variant for requests that will materially exceed latency SLOs; we'll add an X-Redwood-Fallback header so you can detect it.

Plan timeline:
- 09:35 — internal memo and ops ticket created (INF-9421).
- 09:45 — deploy tenant sticky cache and routing to dedicated pool.
- 10:00 — monitor for 60–120 minutes and evaluate p95/p99.
- 12:30 — follow-up with post-mortem and next steps (if needed).

Can you confirm if the product team is OK with the fallback behaviour and whether you'd like us to proceed automatically on threshold breach?

We will keep you posted in this thread and via the incident link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-9421

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2029 12:02:45 -0700
Subject: Exec update: StarryAI p99 tail — mitigation in flight, potential SLA credit discussion

Neha / Laura — summary for execs:

What happened:
- Customer (StarryAI) observed p95/p99 tail latency spikes tied to 16k-context requests starting 2029-05-21T13:30Z. 504s observed but limited.
- Root cause (triage): KV cache churn + increased recompute cost when large-context requests interleave with shared pools.

Actions taken so far:
- Tenant-sticky KV caching enabled at 09:45 PDT; traffic routed to a higher-memory dedicated pool to reduce contention.
- Soft rate-limit for >12k token requests applied (6rps burst cap).
- We offered graceful fallback to 8k model variant with an X-Redwood-Fallback header (customer ok with opt-in).

Current status:
- Early metrics (1.5h into mitigation): p99 for StarryAI dropped from ~3.1s peak to ~850ms; p95 back to ~420ms. No new 504s in last 35 minutes.

Ask:
- If we fail to meet SLA across the 6-hour window, legal/finance will need to evaluate a credit. Please approve outreach and a provisional credit if post-mortem shows platform fault.
- Approval to keep dedicated routing and sticky caching for StarryAI for the next 24–48 hours while we complete a targeted performance patch (cost will be billed to DRI budget unless you advise otherwise).

I've attached the incident ticket and a short PNG of the p99 trend for your review. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-9421

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
